name: reward_clear_final_answer_format
description: Rewards clear, concise final answers in the <solution> tag and penalizes verbose or unclear final answers.

name: reward_correct_integer_final
description: Rewards correct answers, with a small bonus if the final answer is a clean integer when the ground truth is an integer. Penalizes incorrect answers.

name: penalize_repeated_same_number_in_thinking
description: Penalizes thinking blocks where a single number is repeated excessively, which can indicate a stuck generation loop or repetitive checking of the same value.

name: reward_answer_in_thinking
description: Rewards completions where the final numerical answer appears in the thinking block, promoting consistency between reasoning and conclusion.

name: penalize_truncated_thinking
description: Penalizes completions that appear to be truncated, either by having unclosed tags or ending abruptly inside a thinking block with an incomplete equation or sentence.

name: reward_modular_arithmetic_steps
description: Rewards completions that explicitly use modular arithmetic notation and steps, which is essential for problems involving remainders and divisibility (e.g., F7).

name: penalize_brute_force_without_convergence
description: Penalizes completions that engage in extensive brute-force checking (e.g., F1, F3, F4) especially if they appear to be truncated or stuck in a loop without converging to a general solution.

name: penalize_repeated_identical_lines
description: Penalizes completions that have more than 3 consecutive identical lines in the thinking block, indicating a repetitive loop or stuck generation.

name: reward_correct_intermediate_steps
description: Rewards completions that contain multiple equation-based or logical step lines in the thinking process, indicating detailed problem-solving.

name: penalize_off_by_one_errors
description: Penalizes incorrect answers that are very close to the ground truth (off-by-one or simple factor errors), suggesting the model was on the right track but made a minor mistake.

name: reward_step_verification_markers
description: Rewards completions that include explicit verification or conclusion steps in the thinking process, encouraging self-checking and clear reasoning flow.

name: penalize_missing_solution_tag
description: Penalizes completions that are missing the <solution> or <thinking> tags, or have empty tags. Rewards completions that have both non-empty tags.

name: reward_structured_enumeration
description: Rewards completions that use systematic enumeration or case analysis in the thinking block, which is crucial for combinatorial and number theory problems. Penalizes long, unstructured rambling.

name: penalize_missing_structure
description: Rewards completions with both non-empty <thinking> and <solution> tags, and penalizes missing or empty tags.

name: penalize_invalid_latex_structure
description: Penalizes completions with unclosed tags, malformed LaTeX structures (unbalanced brackets/braces), or solutions that are long LaTeX blocks without a clear final numerical answer.

name: penalize_repetitive_loops
description: Penalizes completions that exhibit repetitive looping behavior (e.g., repeating the same number or phrase many times), which is a common failure mode in truncated or stuck generations.

name: penalize_negative_combinatorics
description: Strongly penalizes negative final answers, as they are almost always incorrect in combinatorial counting problems (e.g., F2 where the model calculated a negative number of pairs).

name: penalize_early_truncation
description: Penalizes completions that appear to be truncated, either by being very short without a final answer or by ending abruptly inside a thinking block.

name: penalize_hallucinated_constraints
description: Penalizes long thinking processes that result in very short, incorrect answers, which may indicate the model is overthinking or hallucinating complex steps that don't lead to the correct result.

name: reward_final_answer_clarity
description: Rewards clear, concise final answers in the <solution> tag and penalizes verbose or unclear final answers.

name: reward_consistent_reasoning_length
description: Rewards long thinking that leads to correct answers and penalizes long thinking that leads to wrong answers (potential overthinking/hallucination). Also penalizes short thinking with wrong answers (guessing).

name: penalize_truncated_equations
description: Penalizes completions that appear truncated, specifically those ending with incomplete LaTeX commands or unclosed brackets.

name: reward_complete_thinking_structure
description: Rewards completions that contain both a non-empty <thinking> block and a <solution> block, encouraging structured reasoning before answering.

name: reward_integer_answer_consistency
description: Rewards integer answers and penalizes decimal answers, especially non-integer decimals which are often errors in combinatorics problems.

name: reward_integer_final_for_integer_gt
description: Rewards integer predictions when the ground truth is an integer, and penalizes non-integer predictions in such cases. This addresses common errors in combinatorics and number theory.

name: reward_concise_thinking_for_easy_problems
description: Rewards completions where the length of the thinking block is appropriate for the complexity of the problem. Penalizes overthinking simple problems and underthinking complex ones.

name: reward_correct_intermediate_logic
description: Rewards thinking blocks that contain multiple equation-based steps and logical connectors, indicating structured reasoning.

name: reward_exact_numeric_match
description: Rewards correct answers, with a higher bonus for clean integer formats when the ground truth is an integer. Provides partial credit for numerically close incorrect answers.

name: penalize_unfinished_equations_in_solution
description: Penalizes solutions that contain unfinished or malformed LaTeX equations, such as unclosed brackets or trailing commands, which often occur in truncated outputs.

name: penalize_missing_units_or_context
description: Slightly penalizes solutions that are bare numbers without any explanatory text in the <solution> tag, encouraging more complete answers.

name: penalize_hallucinated_complexity
description: Penalizes long thinking processes that result in short, incorrect answers, which may indicate overthinking or hallucinated complex steps.

name: reward_step_by_step_verification
description: Rewards completions that include explicit verification or conclusion steps in the thinking process, encouraging self-checking.

name: reward_concise_solution_tag
description: Rewards concise final answers in the <solution> tag and penalizes verbose explanations or missing tags.

name: reward_integer_consistency
description: Rewards integer answers when the ground truth is an integer, and penalizes non-integer answers for integer ground truths, addressing common combinatorics errors.

name: reward_final_answer_in_thinking
description: Rewards completions where the final numeric answer appears in the thinking block, promoting consistency between reasoning and conclusion. Penalizes if the final answer is not found in the thinking.

name: penalize_non_integer_result_for_integer_gt
description: Penalizes completions that produce a non-integer final answer when the ground truth is an integer. This addresses failures like F7 where n=242.6667 was predicted for an integer answer.

name: reward_numeric_consistency
description: Rewards completions where the final numerical answer in the <solution> tag also appears in the <thinking> section, promoting consistency between reasoning and conclusion.

name: penalize_obvious_arithmetic_errors
description: Penalizes incorrect answers that are very close to the ground truth (off-by-one or simple factor errors), suggesting the model was on the right track but made a minor mistake.

name: penalize_inconsistent_intermediate_results
description: Penalizes thinking blocks that show sudden, unexplained jumps in numerical magnitude, which often indicate arithmetic errors or hallucinated values (e.g., F2).

name: penalize_repetitive_thinking_lines
description: Penalizes thinking blocks that contain repetitive identical lines, which indicates a stuck or looping generation process.
